factions.description: Europe, Asia north of the Himalayas and North Africa: the largest realm on Earth.

iconicAnimals.name: Plateosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Early long-necked sauropodomorph; mass bone beds at Trossingen, Germany.

iconicAnimals.name: Archaeopteryx
iconicAnimals.description: Feathered dinosaur-bird from the Solnhofen limestone, Bavaria.

iconicAnimals.name: Iguanodon
iconicAnimals.description: Herd-living ornithopod; dozens of skeletons found in a Belgian coal mine at Bernissart.

iconicAnimals.name: Woolly mammoth
iconicAnimals.description: Cold-adapted elephant of the Ice Age mammoth steppe.

factions.description: North America, Greenland and the Mexican highlands.

iconicAnimals.name: Allosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Apex predator of the Morrison Formation floodplains.

iconicAnimals.name: Tyrannosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Giant tyrannosaurid of the latest Cretaceous Hell Creek ecosystem.

iconicAnimals.name: Dawn horse
iconicAnimals.description: Fox-sized early horse from the Eocene of Wyoming.

iconicAnimals.name: Sabre-toothed cat
iconicAnimals.description: Ambush predator preserved by the thousand in the La Brea tar pits.

factions.description: The Indian subcontinent, Indochina, southern China and the Sunda islands (also called Indomalayan).

iconicAnimals.name: Rajasaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Horned abelisaurid from the Narmada valley, when India was an island drifting north.

iconicAnimals.name: Indohyus
iconicAnimals.description: Small Eocene deer-like animal from Kashmir, a close relative of the first whales.

iconicAnimals.name: Sivapithecus
iconicAnimals.description: Miocene ape of the Siwalik Hills, related to orangutans.

iconicAnimals.name: Tiger
iconicAnimals.description: Largest living cat, from the Indian forests to the Sunda islands.

factions.description: Africa south of the Sahara, Madagascar and southern Arabia.

iconicAnimals.name: Gorgonops
iconicAnimals.description: Sabre-toothed gorgonopsian predator of the Karoo Basin, South Africa.

iconicAnimals.name: Massospondylus
iconicAnimals.description: Early sauropodomorph known from nesting sites with embryos in South Africa.

iconicAnimals.name: Lucy's kind
iconicAnimals.description: Upright-walking hominin of the Pliocene Afar region, Ethiopia.

iconicAnimals.name: African bush elephant
iconicAnimals.description: Largest living land animal, shaper of the savanna.

factions.description: South and Central America, the Caribbean and southern Florida.

iconicAnimals.name: Herrerasaurus
iconicAnimals.description: One of the earliest dinosaurs, from the Ischigualasto valley, Argentina.

iconicAnimals.name: Argentinosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Titanosaur, among the heaviest land animals ever.

iconicAnimals.name: Titanoboa
iconicAnimals.description: 13-metre snake from the Paleocene rainforest of Cerrejón, Colombia.

iconicAnimals.name: Terror bird
iconicAnimals.description: Flightless predatory bird of Miocene Patagonia.

iconicAnimals.name: Giant ground sloth
iconicAnimals.description: Elephant-sized sloth of the Pleistocene pampas.

factions.description: Australia, New Guinea, New Zealand and nearby islands east of Wallace's Line.

iconicAnimals.name: Gogonasus
iconicAnimals.description: Lobe-finned fish from the Gogo reef of Western Australia, with limb-like fin bones.

iconicAnimals.name: Muttaburrasaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Large ornithopod of Early Cretaceous Queensland.

iconicAnimals.name: Thunder bird
iconicAnimals.description: Giant flightless mihirung of the Late Miocene.

iconicAnimals.name: Diprotodon
iconicAnimals.description: Rhino-sized wombat relative, the largest marsupial ever.

factions.description: Polynesia, Micronesia and Fiji: volcanic islands and atolls of the Pacific.

iconicAnimals.name: Reef-building corals
iconicAnimals.description: Stony corals, which first appear in the Middle Triassic and later build the Pacific atolls.

iconicAnimals.name: Megalodon
iconicAnimals.description: The largest shark known, cruising the open Pacific in the Miocene and Pliocene.

iconicAnimals.name: Coconut crab
iconicAnimals.description: The largest land arthropod, found on Indo-Pacific islands.

iconicAnimals.name: Nēnē
iconicAnimals.description: Hawaiian goose, descended from Canada geese that reached the islands.

factions.description: Antarctica and the sub-Antarctic islands. Ice-free and forested for most of its history.

iconicAnimals.name: Lystrosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Burrowing dicynodont that survived the end-Permian extinction; found in the Fremouw Formation.

iconicAnimals.name: Cryolophosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Crested predatory dinosaur from Mount Kirkpatrick.

iconicAnimals.name: Colossus penguin
iconicAnimals.description: 1.7 m tall Eocene penguin from Seymour Island.

iconicAnimals.name: Emperor penguin
iconicAnimals.description: Breeds on sea ice through the Antarctic winter.

factions.description: The ancient core of North America, straddling the equator in the early Paleozoic.

iconicAnimals.name: Anomalocaris
iconicAnimals.description: Metre-long radiodont predator of the Burgess Shale, British Columbia.

iconicAnimals.name: Hallucigenia
iconicAnimals.description: Spiny lobopodian worm from the Burgess Shale.

iconicAnimals.name: Isotelus
iconicAnimals.description: The largest complete trilobite, 70 cm long, from Manitoba.

iconicAnimals.name: Sea scorpion
iconicAnimals.description: Eurypterid of the salty lagoons of New York; its state fossil.

factions.description: Scandinavia, the Baltic and western Russia, which drifted from cold southern seas to the tropics.

iconicAnimals.name: Agnostus
iconicAnimals.description: Tiny blind arthropod abundant in the Swedish Alum Shale.

iconicAnimals.name: Stalk-eyed trilobite
iconicAnimals.description: Trilobite with eyes on long stalks, from the St Petersburg region.

iconicAnimals.name: Tremataspis
iconicAnimals.description: Armoured jawless fish from the reefs of Saaremaa, Estonia.

iconicAnimals.name: Panderichthys
iconicAnimals.description: Lobe-finned fish from Latvia, halfway between fish and tetrapod.

factions.description: A microcontinent (eastern Newfoundland, Nova Scotia, England, Wales, Belgium) that crossed the Iapetus Ocean.

iconicAnimals.name: Paradoxides
iconicAnimals.description: Giant trilobite found in both Wales and Newfoundland, early evidence that they were once joined.

iconicAnimals.name: Ogygiocarella
iconicAnimals.description: Trilobite of the Welsh Ordovician seas.

iconicAnimals.name: Dudley bug
iconicAnimals.description: Trilobite of the Wenlock reefs at Dudley, England.

iconicAnimals.name: Hylonomus
iconicAnimals.description: One of the first reptiles, found inside fossil tree stumps at Joggins, Nova Scotia.

factions.description: The Siberian craton, later the heart of Angaraland and the Siberian Traps.

iconicAnimals.name: Archaeocyathids
iconicAnimals.description: Sponge-like animals that built the first animal reefs, along the Lena River.

iconicAnimals.name: Kulindadromeus
iconicAnimals.description: Small feathered plant-eating dinosaur from Transbaikalia.

iconicAnimals.name: Psittacosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Parrot-beaked ceratopsian from Kemerovo, Siberia.

iconicAnimals.name: Woolly rhinoceros
iconicAnimals.description: Shaggy rhino of the Ice Age steppe.

factions.description: The North and South China blocks and Indochina, islands in the Paleo-Tethys.

iconicAnimals.name: Myllokunmingia
iconicAnimals.description: One of the earliest vertebrates, from the Chengjiang biota, Yunnan.

iconicAnimals.name: Guiyu
iconicAnimals.description: Oldest articulated bony fish, from the Late Silurian of Yunnan.

iconicAnimals.name: Keichousaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Small pachypleurosaur reptile of the Guizhou seas, bearing live young.

iconicAnimals.name: Sinosauropteryx
iconicAnimals.description: First non-avian dinosaur found with feathers, from the Jehol biota, Liaoning.

factions.description: The great southern supercontinent: South America, Africa, Antarctica, India and Australia.

iconicAnimals.name: Sacabambaspis
iconicAnimals.description: Jawless armoured fish from Bolivia.

iconicAnimals.name: Mesosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Freshwater reptile found in both Brazil and South Africa, key evidence for continental drift.

iconicAnimals.name: Cynognathus
iconicAnimals.description: Dog-jawed cynodont found in Africa, South America and Antarctica.

iconicAnimals.name: Spinosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Sail-backed semi-aquatic predator of North African rivers.

factions.description: Laurussia, the Old Red Sandstone continent formed when Laurentia, Baltica and Avalonia collided.

iconicAnimals.name: Dunkleosteus
iconicAnimals.description: Armoured placoderm with bony blade jaws, from the Cleveland Shale, Ohio.

iconicAnimals.name: Tiktaalik
iconicAnimals.description: Fish with a neck and wrist-like fins, from Ellesmere Island.

iconicAnimals.name: Arthropleura
iconicAnimals.description: Car-sized millipede of the coal forests.

iconicAnimals.name: Meganeura
iconicAnimals.description: Griffinfly with a 70 cm wingspan, from Commentry, France.

factions.description: The supercontinent that joined nearly all land from the late Paleozoic to the Early Jurassic.

iconicAnimals.name: Dimetrodon
iconicAnimals.description: Sail-backed synapsid, top predator of the Texas red beds.

iconicAnimals.name: Scutosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Armoured pareiasaur of the Russian Permian.

iconicAnimals.name: Coelophysis
iconicAnimals.description: Slender early theropod from Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.

iconicAnimals.name: Dilophosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Double-crested predator of Early Jurassic Arizona.

factions.description: The northern supercontinent left after Pangaea split: North America and Eurasia.

iconicAnimals.name: Megalosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: The first dinosaur ever named (1824), from Oxfordshire, England.

iconicAnimals.name: Velociraptor
iconicAnimals.description: Feathered dromaeosaur of the Gobi Desert.

iconicAnimals.name: Andrewsarchus
iconicAnimals.description: Huge-skulled Eocene mammal of Inner Mongolia.

iconicAnimals.name: Paraceratherium
iconicAnimals.description: Hornless rhino of Oligocene Asia, one of the largest land mammals.

factions.description: The warm tropical ocean between Laurasia and Gondwana; its remnant is the Mediterranean.

iconicAnimals.name: Tanystropheus
iconicAnimals.description: Reptile with a neck longer than its body, from Monte San Giorgio, Switzerland.

iconicAnimals.name: Ichthyosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Dolphin-shaped marine reptile collected by Mary Anning at Lyme Regis.

iconicAnimals.name: Mosasaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Giant marine lizard first found at Maastricht, the Netherlands.

iconicAnimals.name: Basilosaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Serpentine early whale from Wadi Al-Hitan, Egypt.

factions.description: The world ocean surrounding Pangaea; the ancestor of the Pacific.

iconicAnimals.name: Cameroceras
iconicAnimals.description: Giant straight-shelled nautiloid, among the largest Ordovician predators.

iconicAnimals.name: Helicoprion
iconicAnimals.description: Ratfish relative with a spiral whorl of teeth.

iconicAnimals.name: Shonisaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Giant ichthyosaur from Nevada, on the shore of Panthalassa.

iconicAnimals.name: Leedsichthys
iconicAnimals.description: Enormous filter-feeding bony fish.

factions.description: A mostly sunken continent that split from Gondwana; New Zealand is its peak.

iconicAnimals.name: Tuarangisaurus
iconicAnimals.description: Long-necked elasmosaur from the North Island.

iconicAnimals.name: Heracles
iconicAnimals.description: Giant Miocene parrot from St Bathans, about 1 m tall.

iconicAnimals.name: Giant moa
iconicAnimals.description: Flightless bird up to 3.6 m tall with its neck raised.

iconicAnimals.name: Haast's eagle
iconicAnimals.description: The largest eagle known, which hunted moa.
